newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall at open on election fears.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall at open on election fears.

text.p: The French stockmarket's index of leading shares dropped 1.24 percent to 2,516.02 points at Monday's opening, with traders attributing the weakness to political uncertainty ahead of an expected snap general election.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 26.59 points or 1.04 percent at 2,520.97 at 0808 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 25 points at 2,519.
Volume was one billion francs within 20 minutes
There was psychological support seen for the CAC index at 2,500 and below that, at 2,450, which could be the bottom of the consolidation, said one broker.

The market expects President Jacques Chirac to call a snap general election this evening, to seek a mandate to push through austerity measures aimed at qualifying France for a single European currency by 1999.

An election win would boost the market but until the result is in, the market will be in doubt. Financials, dollar stocks and privatisation candidates are seen vulnerable in the climate of political uncertainty.

Weakness in bonds and the franc put banking and financial stocks under pressure, with AGF down 2.26 percent at 190.10, BNP down 1.74 percent at 219.60, and Credit Lyonnais certificates down 5.45 percent at 196.2.
Stocks with heavy dollar exposure, such as Bic, were expected to suffer, on profit-taking as the U.S. currency comes off high against stronger mark.

Privatisation stock Thomson-CSF drops 2.12 percent to 179.8, as election fever was expected to delay the sell-off. Bid candidate Alcatel was down 2.34 percent to 668, while Lagardere was off 1.52 percent to 174.5.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday that planned privatisations of state companies would go ahead if an early general election were called. "All that has been launched will be carried out according to schedule," he told Europe 1 radio.
Market volume was augmented by a block of 1.26 million Coflexip shares changing hands at 314 francs per share, totalling nearly 400 million francs.
Cie Bancaire was among rare risers, adding 0.82 percent to 737. Societe Generale also firm, up 0.16 percent at 617. The two are rumoured to be in link-up talks.
